components.name: Top Bar

components.css: .ds-bar { background: #5b1626; font: 600 14px Manrope, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-bar nav { display: flex; gap: 4px; align-items: center; height: 56px; padding: 0 24px; } .ds-bar b { color: #fff; margin-right: 16px; } .ds-bar a { color: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.78); padding: 6px 10px; border-radius: 6px; } .ds-bar a:hover, .ds-bar a.on { color: #fff; background: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.1); } .ds-bar a span { background: #fff; color: #5b1626; border-radius: 999px; padding: 0 6px; font-size: 12px; } .ds-band { height: 28px; display: flex; align-items: center; padding: 0 24px; color: #1d2b4f; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; background-image: repeating-radial-gradient(circle at 18% 140%, transparent 0 7px, rgb(29 43 79 / 0.09) 7px 8px), repeating-radial-gradient(circle at 82% -40%, transparent 0 9px, rgb(91 22 38 / 0.08) 9px 10px), linear-gradient(90deg, #e3f1e8, #f7e4da); border-bottom: 1px solid #dde1e8; }

narrative.overview:
Every DevvStack console reads like a travel document an inspector trusts. The cover is passport maroon and owns the top bar; under it runs a security band of fine interference rings, captioned with whose document this is (the platform console, or the agency's own name). Pages are plain paper with navy serif titles. The one signature move is the entry stamp: every agency's standing is inked like an immigration stamp, dated, in its status's own colour. Everything else stays quiet, because these are working screens read at a desk for long stretches.

The world lends type, palette, density and the stamp; it never supplies layout, navigation or controls, which stay the standard Flux components every operator already knows. Light and dark themes are both first-class: in dark, the paper turns night navy, the band dims, and the inks brighten to stay legible.
keyCharacteristics: Passport-maroon top bar with a captioned guilloche security band, on every console.
Navy serif titles over a workhorse sans with tabular figures everywhere.
Status shown only as dated entry stamps in six inks; colour is otherwise rare.
Neutrals tinted toward the passport's navy, so every Flux part wears the identity.
Every daily destination on the top bar; counts shown beside what waits.

rules.name: The Ink Means Status Rule
rules.body: A stamp ink appears only where it states an agency's standing (or overdue money in red). Nothing decorative is green, amber, blue, red or violet.

rules.name: The One Cover Rule
rules.body: Maroon covers the top bar and the logo seal. It never fills a button, a card or a badge.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number lines up: the body sets tabular-nums, so money and counts align in every table and figure.

rules.name: The Working Scale Rule
rules.body: Consoles use the scale above. The old 56/48/32px marketing scale is retired; public pages get their own treatment.

rules.name: The Paper Stays Flat Rule
rules.body: Depth is a border, never a shadow. A raised card is a mistake.

dos: Do show every agency status as an entry stamp, never a plain badge.
Do keep colour for meaning: stamp inks for status, red for overdue money, navy for the primary action.
Do set titles in Source Serif 4 and everything else in Manrope with tabular figures.
Do check both themes: every ink and placeholder must pass AA (4.5:1) in light and dark.
Do caption the band with whose console it is (the platform, or the agency's name).
donts: Don't fill buttons, cards or badges with passport maroon.
Don't add shadows for depth; use a hairline border.
Don't rotate or stamp anything except an agency's standing.
Don't bring back the 56/48px headline scale inside a console.
